description: We are Team Yükselen from Antalya, Türkiye: Kaan Oktay, Doruk Yılmaz, Azra İpek Fil, Buğlem Ada Kahramaner and Tunç Serhat Baysal. For the Field Shift challenge we built Tarla Nöbeti, a 3D browser game that turns NASA Earth observations into simple, playable crop rotation decisions for farmers, students and teachers. Try it: https://cemyurtlak.github.io/tarla-nobeti/
summary: Tarla Nöbeti ("Field Watch") is a free 3D browser game and decision-support tool that helps farmers, agriculture students and teachers explore climate-smart crop rotations before they try them in a real field. The player picks a farm anywhere on Earth and runs six 2-hectare parcels month by month: plow, sow, irrigate, fertilize, hoe, spray and harvest 22 crops. Crop growth, water need and frost or heat risk are driven by NASA POWER climate data (temperature, rainfall, solar radiation, frost days and soil wetness) for 68 built-in regions or any point via the live POWER API. A region analysis ranks the best crops for the farmer's own priorities (soil health, water saving, profit), and a sowing calendar shows what fits each month. Soil health, nitrogen, disease and water use change with every decision, so players see why legumes, cover crops and family rotation protect the soil. Five disaster missions based on real events seen by SMAP, GPM IMERG, GRACE-FO, MODIS, Landsat, ECOSTRESS and FIRMS, plus a 2050 climate scenario (+2.2 °C, 15% less rain), test whether today's habits will survive tomorrow's climate. Mistakes are free in the game, which makes NASA Earth observations simple, playable and useful for real farm decisions. Playable in English and Turkish.
details:
What it does

Tarla Nöbeti ("Field Watch") is a decision-support game for climate-smart crop rotation. A farmer, student or teacher picks a farm on a 3D globe and sets three priorities: protect soil, save water, earn profit. The game then simulates the farm month by month with real NASA climate, so the player can test a rotation, see what goes wrong and try again, before risking a real season.

How it works

  • Farm and crops: 6 starting parcels (12 slots, 2 ha each), 22 crops from 10 plant families (cereals, legumes, oilseeds, vegetables, forage, industrial crops and a vetch cover crop), each with sowing months, temperature limits, growing degree-days, water need and nitrogen use.
  • Field work: plow, sow, irrigate, fertilize, hoe, spray, compost and harvest. A water quota, flood / sprinkler / drip irrigation (60 / 75 / 90% efficient), greenhouses and crop insurance make every choice a trade-off.
  • Climate engine: NASA POWER monthly temperature, rainfall, solar radiation, frost days and soil wetness drive crop growth (degree-days), soil water balance and crop water need (FAO-56 Kc values), yield response to water stress (FAO-33), frost and heat damage.
  • Soil and rotation science: soil health, organic matter and nitrogen change with each crop; legumes fix nitrogen, cover crops stop erosion, and repeating one family spreads diseases and pests (yellow rust, late blight, sunn pest, aphids, spider mites) whose spread depends on the weather.
  • Decision support: a region analysis simulates a season of every crop with the local NASA climate and ranks the top crops and market items for the farmer's priorities; a sowing calendar shows what can be sown each month; a "to-do" list flags dry, weedy or nitrogen-poor parcels.
  • Real-year mode: replay a past farming year (2001 onward) using NASA POWER monthly data for the chosen point.
  • Disaster missions and 2050: five missions based on real events (2020–21 Central Anatolia drought, Konya Plain groundwater loss, late spring frost, August 2021 Black Sea floods, summer 2021 heat wave and fires) and a 2050 scenario (+2.2 °C, 15% less rain, 25% lower water quota).
  • Learning and motivation: NASA fact cards and quiz, crop flash cards, 12 quests, 10 badges, a score for soil health, yield, profit and water efficiency, and a village square with comments and a leaderboard.

Benefits and impact

Satellite data is powerful but hard to use for most farmers. Tarla Nöbeti turns it into simple, local answers: what to sow this month, how much water it will need, and how a rotation changes the soil over years. Because mistakes cost nothing in the game, it builds climate literacy for farmers, agriculture students and teachers, and it shows why diverse rotations, legumes and cover crops make farms more resilient to drought, frost, heat and floods.

Tools and technology

A single HTML file (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) that runs in any modern browser on computer, tablet or phone, with no installation. Three.js renders the 3D farm and the globe. A NASA POWER climatology table for 68 regions is built in; for any other point and for real years the game calls the NASA POWER API. Current weather comes from Open-Meteo. The interface is in English and Turkish. Code is public on GitHub: https://github.com/cemyurtlak/tarla-nobeti

What makes it creative

It is a farm simulator where the weather is real NASA data, the disasters are real events seen from space, and the score rewards healthy soil and saved water, not only profit. Players learn rotation by living its results season after season.

Factors we considered

Ease of use for all ages (7 to 70), colour-blind friendly colours, a fast mode for old computers, offline-friendly built-in climate data, honest simplification (disaster events and the 2050 scenario are simplified for the game), and local relevance for Türkiye while working anywhere on Earth.

Use of AI

Claude (Anthropic) assisted the team with code, English translation and presentation text; this is also stated in the code and README. The idea, game design, data choices and testing are the team's own. No AI-generated images are used.
